pending.scope: macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions for AI Pendant Agent
pending.why: The live Mac agent reports ready=false because Accessibility is untrusted and Screen Recording is not granted. These permissions are needed for reliable computer-use/browser vision and end-to-end validation of pendant workflows.
pending.risk: Accessibility permits synthesized input and UI control; Screen Recording permits capturing visible UI. Grant only to the signed AI Pendant Agent app, and retain existing confirmation gates for destructive actions. No permission is needed for read-only health probing itself.
pending.summary: macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions for AI Pendant Agent

pending.why: The owner memory says to ship the 24 kHz superwideband audio path end to end, but reconnaissance only exposes current prototype rates and hardware; it does not specify target codec framing, latency, bandwidth, firmware/relay files in scope, or required validation.
pending.how_it_changes_my_behavior: With the acceptance criteria I can propose or implement a bounded firmware/relay change and select meaningful build/audio integration tests instead of guessing what 'superwideband' means.

pending.name: mac_workspace_edit
pending.why: The owner's stated goal is to ship the 24 kHz superwideband pendant audio path end-to-end. Reconnaissance shows mismatched 15,625 Hz capture/16 kHz uplink, 24 kHz decode, and 31,250 Hz I2S; implementing and validating this requires editing firmware and relay source files in ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace, then running builds/tests without relying on destructive GUI automation.

commands.description: Allowlisted build/test commands to run after edits

dry_run.description: If true, show proposed diffs and commands without writing or executing

pending.expected_output: Structured result containing per-file diff status, command stdout/stderr/exit codes, and artifact paths; no write or command execution when dry_run=true.

pending.name: audio_pipeline_validate
pending.why: The owner’s stated goal is to ship the 24 kHz superwideband path end to end. Reconnaissance confirms 24 kHz WAV output, but we lack a safe, read-only validator that checks capture→relay→TTS→pendant/bridge formats, resampling, frame timing, clipping, and round-trip continuity against the acceptance criteria.

pipeline_id.description: Existing pipeline run ID to validate; if omitted, choose the newest completed audio run.

checks.description: Checks to perform; defaults to all safe checks.

pending.why: Current measured path cannot be native 24 kHz end-to-end: nRF capture is 15.625 kHz, uplink Opus is 16 kHz, bridge is fixed SBC 44.1 kHz, and LTE contention drops speech packets. I need to know whether this round should optimize the existing prototype or specify a product-level hardware/codec redesign.
pending.how_it_changes_my_behavior: If product redesign is intended, I will prioritize an architecture/acceptance plan (mic/codec, transport bitrate, bridge replacement, clocks, latency, packet-loss behavior). If prototype-only is intended, I will constrain work to firmware/relay resampling and measurable pipeline validation within the existing I2S and LTE limits.

pending.why: Owner memory projects America/Chicago but the live Mac machine-context reports America/New_York; this affects routines, reminders, and any audio-path acceptance timestamps.
pending.how_it_changes_my_behavior: I will use the confirmed timezone for scheduling and interpret pipeline timestamps consistently; until clarified I will not alter schedules or claim local-time correctness.

result.note: These are the Mac agent routes. Your own backend may differ — probe_http hits whichever backend you run against.

result.name: get_mac_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Read live Mac device state: battery, wifi, volume, focused app, or all. Use when the owner asks about battery/charge, wifi/network, volume/mute, or what app is frontmost. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: controlling the Mac (open app, set volume, type, reminders — use mac_run_actions), browser work (browser_run_actions), public web facts (web_search), or multi-step ambiguous tasks (mac_delegate). Never invent readings; always call this tool instead of guessing numbers.

fields.description: Optional status fields to fetch. Omit or use ["all"] for a full snapshot.

spoken_reply.description: Short pendant confirmation (e.g. "Checking battery."). One sentence.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: mac_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE for reversible control. Execute 1–3 concrete Mac actions when the Mac surface is online: open_app, open_url, open_path, create_reminder, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, run_shell (allowlisted system intents), run_applescript, and similar. Prefer high-level types over raw shell when a typed action exists. Use when: owner wants to change or run something on the Mac that is not a pure status read. Do NOT use when: only reading battery/wifi/volume/focused app (get_mac_status), browser page work (browser_run_actions), public facts (web_search), or long multi-step ambiguous workflows (mac_delegate). Confirmation first only for destructive actions. Never claim success without this tool (or get_mac_status) actually queuing work.

actions.description: 1–3 concrete actions for the Mac executor (primary product of this tool).

type.description: Executor action type. Examples: run_shell, run_applescript, create_reminder, open_app, open_url, open_path, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, browser_snapshot, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select.

label.description: Short human-readable label for logs / UI.

params.description: Parameters for the action type. Use only fields that type needs (e.g. command for run_shell, title/due for create_reminder, url for open_url or browser_navigate, selector/text for browser_click/type, appName for open_app matching the Mac software inventory exactly).

spoken_reply.description: Short confirmation for the pendant speaker (preferred user-facing reply).

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure — never block on this; plan from audio via actions.

result.name: mac_delegate
result.description: ONLY for multi-step or ambiguous computer tasks that cannot fit a short action list. Hands the goal to the local Mac agent (sets requireLocalPlanner). Use when: complex multi-app workflows, unclear steps, long-running computer use. Do NOT use when: a single get_mac_status or 1–3 mac_run_actions / browser_run_actions would suffice. Prefer concrete tools first.

goal.description: Clear goal for the Mac agent to accomplish.

spoken_reply.description: Optional short confirmation for the pendant speaker while the Mac works.

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.note: NOTE RE-DERIVED 2026-08-07. The previous agent's 4,452-char patch plan was DESTROYED when this entry was set to "implementing": scripts/harness-ledger.mjs status --note overwrites the note, it does not append. Every claim below was re-verified against the live files today; the headline claim holds and is worse than it was stated. HEADLINE (TRUE): the sweeper cannot clear a backlog. audioRetention.js:171-175 lists with limit Math.min(Math.max(n,1),100) and passes no cursor; store/jobQuery.js:8 JOB_LIST_MAX_LIMIT = 100 clamps it again, so raising the local constant alone fixes nothing. Ordering is newest-first on both stores (store/d1Store.js:566 ORDER BY created_at DESC; store/memoryStore.js:166). The sweep therefore only ever inspects the 100 NEWEST audio_capture rows — the ones least likely to be expired — and repeated runs never advance the window. A keyset cursor already exists and is plumbed through listJobs({before}) (store/jobQuery.js:19-37, used at server.js:1893); sweepExpiredAudio simply never passes it. OTHER VERIFIED GAPS. (2) AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_MAX_BATCH = 200 at audioRetention.js:32 is unreachable dead config given the 100 cap. (3) No scheduled invocation exists: cloudflare-worker/worker.js exports only fetch, wrangler.jsonc has no crons/triggers, and the sole caller is the manual route at server.js:2151. (4) Inert as shipped: wrangler.jsonc:34 sets AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_ENABLED=false and server.js:2149 forces dryRun, so the deployed sweeper deletes nothing under any input. (5) Bindings are not threaded into either delete path: server.js:2151 and server.js:2834 call without bindings, and cloudflareBindings is only populated inside the Worker fetch handler — under plain Node deleteAudioCaptureObject short-circuits false (audioStorage.js:130-136), so the D1 pointer is cleared at audioRetention.js:141-147 while the R2 object is orphaned permanently, and the response still returns ok:true. (6) Non-atomic ordering: the R2 delete precedes the pointer clear, so an updateJob throw leaves a row addressing a deleted object. (7) In record mode with no store.deleteJob the object is already gone while the row keeps a stale audioRef; that branch has no test. (8) One R2 error aborts the whole sweep: audioRetention.js:195-204 is an unguarded loop with no per-item try/catch and no partial report. (9) NO owner-pin concept exists anywhere in cloud-relay — the entry's "keep owner-pinned items separate with an explicit expiry" is 0% implemented. (10) One global 30-day TTL (config.js:27-31, wrangler.jsonc:33); generated agent audio is an ordinary audio_capture row tagged role:reply (server.js:1075), so "short retention for generated briefings" is not implemented and there is no briefing concept in cloud-relay at all. (11) DELETE /v1/ops/history/:pipelineId/audio (server.js:1979-1995) never follows replyCaptureId, so deleting a run leaves the synthesized reply audio in R2 — and record mode destroys the only reference to it. (12) No dashboard reaches either delete route: src/ops/api.js has no audio DELETE and no retention call at all, so the "dashboard delete now action" does not exist in the frontend. (13) The read-only report at server.js:2115 hardcodes limit 100, so storedRecordings and expiredCount are structurally wrong past 100 captures. (14) The sweep report calls captures.length "scanned" (audioRetention.js:182,209), implying a full-corpus scan that never happened. NO DEFECT FOUND on clock/units: createdAt is ISO-8601 wherever written (jobs.js:20,34-35), parsed with Date.getTime (audioRetention.js:62) and compared against ms Date.now (audioRetention.js:78,86); maxAgeMs is milliseconds in config.js:27, in wrangler.jsonc:33 (2592000000 = 30d) and in the comparison alike. TEST GAPS: audioRetention.test.js never exercises a backlog >100 through a real store (the batch-cap test calls selectExpiredAudioCaptures on a plain array, bypassing listJobs, so gap 1 is invisible to the suite and gap 2 is asserted as correct), never makes an R2 delete throw, and always passes bindings explicitly — which is precisely what production does not do. cloud-relay/ was NOT edited. Left proposed.

result.name: get_mac_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Read live Mac device state: battery, wifi, volume, focused app, or all. Use when the owner asks about battery/charge, wifi/network, volume/mute, or what app is frontmost. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: controlling the Mac (open app, set volume, type, reminders — use mac_run_actions), browser work (browser_run_actions), public web facts (web_search), or multi-step ambiguous tasks (mac_delegate). Never invent readings; always call this tool instead of guessing numbers.

fields.description: Optional status fields to fetch. Omit or use ["all"] for a full snapshot.

spoken_reply.description: Short pendant confirmation (e.g. "Checking battery."). One sentence.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: mac_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE for reversible control. Execute 1–3 concrete Mac actions when the Mac surface is online: open_app, open_url, open_path, create_reminder, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, run_shell (allowlisted system intents), run_applescript, and similar. Prefer high-level types over raw shell when a typed action exists. Use when: owner wants to change or run something on the Mac that is not a pure status read. Do NOT use when: only reading battery/wifi/volume/focused app (get_mac_status), browser page work (browser_run_actions), public facts (web_search), or long multi-step ambiguous workflows (mac_delegate). Confirmation first only for destructive actions. Never claim success without this tool (or get_mac_status) actually queuing work.

actions.description: 1–3 concrete actions for the Mac executor (primary product of this tool).

type.description: Executor action type. Examples: run_shell, run_applescript, create_reminder, open_app, open_url, open_path, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, browser_snapshot, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select.

label.description: Short human-readable label for logs / UI.

params.description: Parameters for the action type. Use only fields that type needs (e.g. command for run_shell, title/due for create_reminder, url for open_url or browser_navigate, selector/text for browser_click/type, appName for open_app matching the Mac software inventory exactly).

spoken_reply.description: Short confirmation for the pendant speaker (preferred user-facing reply).

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure — never block on this; plan from audio via actions.

result.name: browser_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE when browser work is needed. Execute 1–3 actions through the browser extension when online: browser_list_tabs, browser_snapshot, browser_navigate, browser_click/type by ref, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select, scroll. Use when: web/logged-in site work, reading or interacting with a page. Do NOT use when: Mac desktop/system control (mac_run_actions / get_mac_status), public web facts without a page (web_search), or multi-step Mac workflows (mac_delegate). Prefer over Mac desktop control for in-browser tasks.

actions.description: 1–3 browser-extension actions (primary product of this tool).

type.description: Executor action type. Examples: run_shell, run_applescript, create_reminder, open_app, open_url, open_path, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, browser_snapshot, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select.

label.description: Short human-readable label for logs / UI.

params.description: Parameters for the action type. Use only fields that type needs (e.g. command for run_shell, title/due for create_reminder, url for open_url or browser_navigate, selector/text for browser_click/type, appName for open_app matching the Mac software inventory exactly).

spoken_reply.description: Short confirmation for the pendant speaker (preferred user-facing reply).

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.relay: Cloudflare Worker (Express-style). D1 for jobs/history/memory, R2 for audio. Audio retention 30 days, sweep disabled, ~100 recordings stored.
result.agent_tools_today: The realtime agent currently has exactly 5 tools: get_mac_status, mac_run_actions, browser_run_actions, web_search, mac_delegate.
result.mac_harness: A Node "local agent" on the owner's Mac: planner (gpt-5.6-luna), computer-use loop, browser bridge, action risk scoring, atomic JSON store, context graph. It polls /v1/bridge/work for jobs and posts results back.
result.browser_harness: Driven through the Mac agent's browser bridge today. Cloudflare Browser Run now exists and could give the relay its own server-side browser, removing the Mac from web tasks entirely.
result.clients: ONE SvelteKit dashboard renders on all three surfaces: web, a Swift menubar app via WKWebView, and iOS via Capacitor pointed at the same Worker URL. A change to the web app ships to all three.
result.memory: Knowledge-graph style store behind /v1/ops/memory: entities, relations, sessions. Separately, fleetContext.js hand-writes a prompt section per surface, which means adding a surface means editing a prompt.

result.button: ONE user button, devicetree alias sw0. Press starts a conversation; second press ends it. It is also pokable over J-Link for testing.
result.led: ONE LED, alias led0. Currently signals recording, stays solid while agent audio is buffered, and flashes error codes.
result.buses: GPIO, I2C, SPI and I2S all enabled (prj.conf). I2C and SPI are FREE — nothing is attached to them today.
result.caution: There is exactly one I2S peripheral and it runs full duplex (mic in + speaker out) with byte-identical TX/RX config. Any new audio path must share it.

transcript.text:
Environment reconnaissance completed.

What I established:

- **Mac agent:** Local agent v0.5.0 is live and reachable; relay connectivity is healthy.
- **Browser:** Browser extension is currently offline, with no connected devices.
- **Permissions:** Accessibility and Screen Recording are still not granted; computer-use loop is disabled. Automation grants exist for major apps.
- **Pendant audio mismatch:**  
  - Microphone capture: **15,625 Hz**
  - Uplink Opus: **16 kHz / 16 kbps**
  - Playback decode: **24 kHz**
  - Pendant I2S wire clock: **31,250 Hz**
  - Relay TTS already produces **24 kHz mono PCM**
- **Hardware constraints:** nRF9160 DK prototype, 64 MHz Cortex-M33, about 211 KB application RAM, one full-duplex I2S peripheral. ESP32 bridge resamples 31,250→44,100 and uses SBC-only A2DP.
- **Relay:** v1.1.0, reachable, paired, speech-to-text and durable audio enabled. Audio retention is 30 days, sweeping disabled, with approximately 100 recordings stored.
- **Owner preferences:** America/Chicago timezone, concise spoken replies, browser reading/clicking permitted, confirmation required for destructive actions, workspace at `~/AI-Pendant-Workspace`.

I recorded these findings and requested the missing **workspace-edit/build capability** needed to implement and test the audio-path changes. The request is queued as `t2-h6u8`.

Still needed before useful implementation work:

1. The previously requested `mac_workspace_edit` capability.
2. Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions for the AI Pendant Agent.
3. The previously requested **24 kHz superwideband acceptance criteria**.
4. Source-level inspection of the firmware and relay audio files, followed by a build/test run once editing access is available.

The main unresolved technical question is whether “24 kHz end-to-end” means changing capture and I2S clocks to true 24 kHz, or preserving the existing 31,250 Hz electrical clock while carrying a 24 kHz logical PCM stream.

result.name: get_mac_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Read live Mac device state: battery, wifi, volume, focused app, or all. Use when the owner asks about battery/charge, wifi/network, volume/mute, or what app is frontmost. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: controlling the Mac (open app, set volume, type, reminders — use mac_run_actions), browser work (browser_run_actions), public web facts (web_search), or multi-step ambiguous tasks (mac_delegate). Never invent readings; always call this tool instead of guessing numbers.

fields.description: Optional status fields to fetch. Omit or use ["all"] for a full snapshot.

spoken_reply.description: Short pendant confirmation (e.g. "Checking battery."). One sentence.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: mac_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE for reversible control. Execute 1–3 concrete Mac actions when the Mac surface is online: open_app, open_url, open_path, create_reminder, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, run_shell (allowlisted system intents), run_applescript, and similar. Prefer high-level types over raw shell when a typed action exists. Use when: owner wants to change or run something on the Mac that is not a pure status read. Do NOT use when: only reading battery/wifi/volume/focused app (get_mac_status), browser page work (browser_run_actions), public facts (web_search), or long multi-step ambiguous workflows (mac_delegate). Confirmation first only for destructive actions. Never claim success without this tool (or get_mac_status) actually queuing work.

actions.description: 1–3 concrete actions for the Mac executor (primary product of this tool).

type.description: Executor action type. Examples: run_shell, run_applescript, create_reminder, open_app, open_url, open_path, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, browser_snapshot, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select.

label.description: Short human-readable label for logs / UI.

params.description: Parameters for the action type. Use only fields that type needs (e.g. command for run_shell, title/due for create_reminder, url for open_url or browser_navigate, selector/text for browser_click/type, appName for open_app matching the Mac software inventory exactly).

spoken_reply.description: Short confirmation for the pendant speaker (preferred user-facing reply).

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure — never block on this; plan from audio via actions.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: get_mac_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Read live Mac device state: battery, wifi, volume, focused app, or all. Use when the owner asks about battery/charge, wifi/network, volume/mute, or what app is frontmost. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: controlling the Mac (open app, set volume, type, reminders — use mac_run_actions), browser work (browser_run_actions), public web facts (web_search), or multi-step ambiguous tasks (mac_delegate). Never invent readings; always call this tool instead of guessing numbers.

fields.description: Optional status fields to fetch. Omit or use ["all"] for a full snapshot.

spoken_reply.description: Short pendant confirmation (e.g. "Checking battery."). One sentence.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: mac_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE for reversible control. Execute 1–3 concrete Mac actions when the Mac surface is online: open_app, open_url, open_path, create_reminder, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, run_shell (allowlisted system intents), run_applescript, and similar. Prefer high-level types over raw shell when a typed action exists. Use when: owner wants to change or run something on the Mac that is not a pure status read. Do NOT use when: only reading battery/wifi/volume/focused app (get_mac_status), browser page work (browser_run_actions), public facts (web_search), or long multi-step ambiguous workflows (mac_delegate). Confirmation first only for destructive actions. Never claim success without this tool (or get_mac_status) actually queuing work.

actions.description: 1–3 concrete actions for the Mac executor (primary product of this tool).

type.description: Executor action type. Examples: run_shell, run_applescript, create_reminder, open_app, open_url, open_path, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, browser_snapshot, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select.

label.description: Short human-readable label for logs / UI.

params.description: Parameters for the action type. Use only fields that type needs (e.g. command for run_shell, title/due for create_reminder, url for open_url or browser_navigate, selector/text for browser_click/type, appName for open_app matching the Mac software inventory exactly).

spoken_reply.description: Short confirmation for the pendant speaker (preferred user-facing reply).

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure — never block on this; plan from audio via actions.

result.name: browser_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE when browser work is needed. Execute 1–3 actions through the browser extension when online: browser_list_tabs, browser_snapshot, browser_navigate, browser_click/type by ref, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select, scroll. Use when: web/logged-in site work, reading or interacting with a page. Do NOT use when: Mac desktop/system control (mac_run_actions / get_mac_status), public web facts without a page (web_search), or multi-step Mac workflows (mac_delegate). Prefer over Mac desktop control for in-browser tasks.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

pendant.board: Nordic nRF9160 DK (nRF9160 SiP), non-secure app under TF-M minimal
pendant.cpu: Arm Cortex-M33 @ 64 MHz, DSP extension present (libopus ARMv5E paths apply)
pendant.ram: 211,608 B application RAM (boards/nrf9160dk_nrf9160_ns.overlay); 32 kB secure, modem shares the first 128 kB
pendant.flash: 1 MB total; application text ~316 kB with libopus at -O3

io.button: ONE user button, devicetree alias sw0. Press starts a conversation; second press ends it. It is also pokable over J-Link for testing.
io.led: ONE LED, alias led0. Currently signals recording, stays solid while agent audio is buffered, and flashes error codes.
io.buses: GPIO, I2C, SPI and I2S all enabled (prj.conf). I2C and SPI are FREE — nothing is attached to them today.
io.caution: There is exactly one I2S peripheral and it runs full duplex (mic in + speaker out) with byte-identical TX/RX config. Any new audio path must share it.

storage.sd: microSD over SPI. CONFIG_DISK_DRIVER_SDMMC, FATFS (ELM) with exFAT enabled. Mount is FS_FATFS.
storage.policy: Owner's standing rule: audio is written to SD ONLY when a chunk upload cannot be uploaded. It is a failure buffer, not a routine store.
storage.note: exFAT means large files and long filenames are available.

audio.mic: I2S microphone, 15,625 Hz capture, Opus-encoded uplink at 16 kHz / 16 kbps, complexity 0
audio.playback: Opus decode on-device at 24 kHz / 60 ms frames, resampled to the 31,250 Hz I2S wire clock, out to the ESP32 bridge
audio.codec: libopus 1.6.1 vendored, fixed-point, built -O3. Decode ~25.4 ms per 60 ms packet; encode ~15.0 ms per call. Roughly 87% of one core when both run.

bridge.board: Adafruit HUZZAH32 (ESP32 classic), 240 MHz dual core, 320 kB DRAM
bridge.role: Receives I2S from the pendant, resamples 31250 -> 44100 with a polyphase FIR, and is an A2DP SOURCE to Bluetooth headphones
bridge.limit: A2DP source is SBC-only and hard-locked to 44.1 kHz stereo in the precompiled bluedroid. RAM is tight: a 44 kB buffer once starved the Bluetooth stack into silence.

network.link: LTE-M (Cat-M1) via the nRF9160 modem. Half duplex in practice.
network.transport: One TLS WebSocket to the Cloudflare Worker carries uplink and downlink audio simultaneously. Modem TLS record limit is about 2 kB.
network.measured: Uplink 16 kbps + downlink 24 kbps saturates the link under contention: a recent call dropped 388 uplink packets (~7.8 s of speech) when the agent was speaking at the same time the owner was.

stack.relay: Cloudflare Worker (Express-style). D1 for jobs/history/memory, R2 for audio. Audio retention 30 days, sweep disabled, ~100 recordings stored.
stack.agent_tools_today: The realtime agent currently has exactly 5 tools: get_mac_status, mac_run_actions, browser_run_actions, web_search, mac_delegate.
stack.mac_harness: A Node "local agent" on the owner's Mac: planner (gpt-5.6-luna), computer-use loop, browser bridge, action risk scoring, atomic JSON store, context graph. It polls /v1/bridge/work for jobs and posts results back.
stack.browser_harness: Driven through the Mac agent's browser bridge today. Cloudflare Browser Run now exists and could give the relay its own server-side browser, removing the Mac from web tasks entirely.
stack.clients: ONE SvelteKit dashboard renders on all three surfaces: web, a Swift menubar app via WKWebView, and iOS via Capacitor pointed at the same Worker URL. A change to the web app ships to all three.
stack.memory: Knowledge-graph style store behind /v1/ops/memory: entities, relations, sessions. Separately, fleetContext.js hand-writes a prompt section per surface, which means adding a surface means editing a prompt.

power.supply: USB or battery. LTE-M transmit bursts draw far more than idle.
power.note: No battery gauge is wired up today, so the agent cannot read charge state.

result.status: PROTOTYPE. This is a Nordic development kit, not the product. Every choice here — the SoC, the RAM, the single button, the single LED, the enclosure — is provisional and can change. Design the device the owner should wear, then say what it would take to build it.
result.you_are_here: You run on the owner's MacBook (unified). Every device described here is REMOTE to you — you are not running on the pendant or the ESP32.

result.note: These are the Mac agent routes. Your own backend may differ — probe_http hits whichever backend you run against.

result.name: get_mac_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Read live Mac device state: battery, wifi, volume, focused app, or all. Use when the owner asks about battery/charge, wifi/network, volume/mute, or what app is frontmost. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: controlling the Mac (open app, set volume, type, reminders — use mac_run_actions), browser work (browser_run_actions), public web facts (web_search), or multi-step ambiguous tasks (mac_delegate). Never invent readings; always call this tool instead of guessing numbers.

fields.description: Optional status fields to fetch. Omit or use ["all"] for a full snapshot.

spoken_reply.description: Short pendant confirmation (e.g. "Checking battery."). One sentence.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: mac_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE for reversible control. Execute 1–3 concrete Mac actions when the Mac surface is online: open_app, open_url, open_path, create_reminder, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, run_shell (allowlisted system intents), run_applescript, and similar. Prefer high-level types over raw shell when a typed action exists. Use when: owner wants to change or run something on the Mac that is not a pure status read. Do NOT use when: only reading battery/wifi/volume/focused app (get_mac_status), browser page work (browser_run_actions), public facts (web_search), or long multi-step ambiguous workflows (mac_delegate). Confirmation first only for destructive actions. Never claim success without this tool (or get_mac_status) actually queuing work.

actions.description: 1–3 concrete actions for the Mac executor (primary product of this tool).

type.description: Executor action type. Examples: run_shell, run_applescript, create_reminder, open_app, open_url, open_path, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, browser_snapshot, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select.

label.description: Short human-readable label for logs / UI.

params.description: Parameters for the action type. Use only fields that type needs (e.g. command for run_shell, title/due for create_reminder, url for open_url or browser_navigate, selector/text for browser_click/type, appName for open_app matching the Mac software inventory exactly).

spoken_reply.description: Short confirmation for the pendant speaker (preferred user-facing reply).

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure — never block on this; plan from audio via actions.

result.name: browser_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE when browser work is needed. Execute 1–3 actions through the browser extension when online: browser_list_tabs, browser_snapshot, browser_navigate, browser_click/type by ref, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select, scroll. Use when: web/logged-in site work, reading or interacting with a page. Do NOT use when: Mac desktop/system control (mac_run_actions / get_mac_status), public web facts without a page (web_search), or multi-step Mac workflows (mac_delegate). Prefer over Mac desktop control for in-browser tasks.

actions.description: 1–3 browser-extension actions (primary product of this tool).

type.description: Executor action type. Examples: run_shell, run_applescript, create_reminder, open_app, open_url, open_path, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, browser_snapshot, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select.

label.description: Short human-readable label for logs / UI.

params.description: Parameters for the action type. Use only fields that type needs (e.g. command for run_shell, title/due for create_reminder, url for open_url or browser_navigate, selector/text for browser_click/type, appName for open_app matching the Mac software inventory exactly).

spoken_reply.description: Short confirmation for the pendant speaker (preferred user-facing reply).

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.board: Nordic nRF9160 DK (nRF9160 SiP), non-secure app under TF-M minimal
result.cpu: Arm Cortex-M33 @ 64 MHz, DSP extension present (libopus ARMv5E paths apply)
result.ram: 211,608 B application RAM (boards/nrf9160dk_nrf9160_ns.overlay); 32 kB secure, modem shares the first 128 kB
result.flash: 1 MB total; application text ~316 kB with libopus at -O3

result.mic: I2S microphone, 15,625 Hz capture, Opus-encoded uplink at 16 kHz / 16 kbps, complexity 0
result.playback: Opus decode on-device at 24 kHz / 60 ms frames, resampled to the 31,250 Hz I2S wire clock, out to the ESP32 bridge
result.codec: libopus 1.6.1 vendored, fixed-point, built -O3. Decode ~25.4 ms per 60 ms packet; encode ~15.0 ms per call. Roughly 87% of one core when both run.

result.relay: Cloudflare Worker (Express-style). D1 for jobs/history/memory, R2 for audio. Audio retention 30 days, sweep disabled, ~100 recordings stored.
result.agent_tools_today: The realtime agent currently has exactly 5 tools: get_mac_status, mac_run_actions, browser_run_actions, web_search, mac_delegate.
result.mac_harness: A Node "local agent" on the owner's Mac: planner (gpt-5.6-luna), computer-use loop, browser bridge, action risk scoring, atomic JSON store, context graph. It polls /v1/bridge/work for jobs and posts results back.
result.browser_harness: Driven through the Mac agent's browser bridge today. Cloudflare Browser Run now exists and could give the relay its own server-side browser, removing the Mac from web tasks entirely.
result.clients: ONE SvelteKit dashboard renders on all three surfaces: web, a Swift menubar app via WKWebView, and iOS via Capacitor pointed at the same Worker URL. A change to the web app ships to all three.
result.memory: Knowledge-graph style store behind /v1/ops/memory: entities, relations, sessions. Separately, fleetContext.js hand-writes a prompt section per surface, which means adding a surface means editing a prompt.

result.link: LTE-M (Cat-M1) via the nRF9160 modem. Half duplex in practice.
result.transport: One TLS WebSocket to the Cloudflare Worker carries uplink and downlink audio simultaneously. Modem TLS record limit is about 2 kB.
result.measured: Uplink 16 kbps + downlink 24 kbps saturates the link under contention: a recent call dropped 388 uplink packets (~7.8 s of speech) when the agent was speaking at the same time the owner was.

transcript.text:
Reconnaissance completed. Current environment:

- **Mac bridge:** Online at `localhost:8000`, agent v0.5.0, bearer authentication configured.
- **Relay:** Reachable and paired; Cloudflare Worker v1.1.0 with D1/R2, speech-to-text, durable audio, and pendant telemetry.
- **Pendant:** nRF9160 Cortex-M33, Zephyr/NCS 3.4.0, 211,608 B application RAM, 1 MB flash.
- **Audio path:** 15,625 Hz microphone capture; 16 kHz/16 kbps Opus uplink; 24 kHz/60 ms Opus downlink decoded and resampled to 31,250 Hz I2S. A recent trace successfully produced 24 kHz mono PCM with no clipping.
- **Known audio risk:** LTE-M contention is severe: simultaneous uplink/downlink previously dropped about 7.8 seconds of speech.
- **Browser:** Currently offline, with zero connected devices and five pending commands.
- **Mac readiness:** `ready=false`; Accessibility is untrusted and Screen Recording is not granted. Automation grants are present, but these two permissions still block reliable GUI/computer-use operation.
- **Other devices:** The mobile contract-test device is offline.
- **Retention:** Audio retention is nominally 30 days, but the R2/D1 cleanup sweep is disabled and roughly 100 recordings exist.

What I still need for useful implementation work:

1. The previously requested **macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording grants** for AI Pendant Agent.
2. The previously requested **workspace-edit capability** to modify the firmware/relay workspace.
3. The previously requested **audio pipeline validation capability**.
4. The pending **24 kHz superwideband acceptance criteria**, especially packet-loss, latency, jitter, clipping, and behavior during LTE-M contention.

I did not repeat those requests because they were already pending.

result.name: get_mac_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Read live Mac device state: battery, wifi, volume, focused app, or all. Use when the owner asks about battery/charge, wifi/network, volume/mute, or what app is frontmost. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: controlling the Mac (open app, set volume, type, reminders — use mac_run_actions), browser work (browser_run_actions), public web facts (web_search), or multi-step ambiguous tasks (mac_delegate). Never invent readings; always call this tool instead of guessing numbers.

fields.description: Optional status fields to fetch. Omit or use ["all"] for a full snapshot.

spoken_reply.description: Short pendant confirmation (e.g. "Checking battery."). One sentence.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: mac_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE for reversible control. Execute 1–3 concrete Mac actions when the Mac surface is online: open_app, open_url, open_path, create_reminder, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, run_shell (allowlisted system intents), run_applescript, and similar. Prefer high-level types over raw shell when a typed action exists. Use when: owner wants to change or run something on the Mac that is not a pure status read. Do NOT use when: only reading battery/wifi/volume/focused app (get_mac_status), browser page work (browser_run_actions), public facts (web_search), or long multi-step ambiguous workflows (mac_delegate). Confirmation first only for destructive actions. Never claim success without this tool (or get_mac_status) actually queuing work.

actions.description: 1–3 concrete actions for the Mac executor (primary product of this tool).

type.description: Executor action type. Examples: run_shell, run_applescript, create_reminder, open_app, open_url, open_path, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, browser_snapshot, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select.

label.description: Short human-readable label for logs / UI.

params.description: Parameters for the action type. Use only fields that type needs (e.g. command for run_shell, title/due for create_reminder, url for open_url or browser_navigate, selector/text for browser_click/type, appName for open_app matching the Mac software inventory exactly).

spoken_reply.description: Short confirmation for the pendant speaker (preferred user-facing reply).

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure — never block on this; plan from audio via actions.

result.name: browser_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE when browser work is needed. Execute 1–3 actions through the browser extension when online: browser_list_tabs, browser_snapshot, browser_navigate, browser_click/type by ref, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select, scroll. Use when: web/logged-in site work, reading or interacting with a page. Do NOT use when: Mac desktop/system control (mac_run_actions / get_mac_status), public web facts without a page (web_search), or multi-step Mac workflows (mac_delegate). Prefer over Mac desktop control for in-browser tasks.

actions.description: 1–3 browser-extension actions (primary product of this tool).

type.description: Executor action type. Examples: run_shell, run_applescript, create_reminder, open_app, open_url, open_path, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, browser_snapshot, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select.

label.description: Short human-readable label for logs / UI.

params.description: Parameters for the action type. Use only fields that type needs (e.g. command for run_shell, title/due for create_reminder, url for open_url or browser_navigate, selector/text for browser_click/type, appName for open_app matching the Mac software inventory exactly).

spoken_reply.description: Short confirmation for the pendant speaker (preferred user-facing reply).

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: web_search
result.description: PROACTIVE for live public facts. Look up current information on the public web (news, weather, sports, prices, anything that needs live data). Use when: answer needs up-to-date public information. Do NOT use when: Mac device state (get_mac_status), controlling Mac/browser (mac_run_actions / browser_run_actions), or pure knowledge you already know without live data.

query.description: Search query derived from the user speech.

result.name: read_web_page
result.description: PROACTIVE for reading a specific public web page without the Mac. Fetches one public URL with a cloud browser on the relay and returns its readable text — works when the Mac is asleep, closed, or offline. Use when: the owner names a page/site/article to read, or web_search returned a link whose contents you now need. Do NOT use when: the page needs the owner's login, is on their home network, or must be clicked/typed into — that browser has no sessions and no LAN access, so use browser_run_actions (Mac extension) instead. Do NOT use for open-ended lookups with no page in mind (web_search) or Mac state (get_mac_status). Read-only: it cannot click, type, or submit.

url.description: Full public URL to read (a bare hostname like "example.com" is fine).

spoken_reply.description: Short pendant confirmation (e.g. "Reading that page."). One sentence.

result.playback: Opus decode on-device at 24 kHz / 60 ms frames, resampled to the 31,250 Hz I2S wire clock, out to the ESP32 bridge
result.codec: libopus 1.6.1 vendored, fixed-point, built -O3. Decode ~25.4 ms per 60 ms packet; encode ~15.0 ms per call. Roughly 87% of one core when both run.

result.memory: Knowledge-graph style store behind /v1/ops/memory: entities, relations, sessions. Separately, fleetContext.js hand-writes a prompt section per surface, which means adding a surface means editing a prompt.

pendant.board: Nordic nRF9160 DK (nRF9160 SiP), non-secure app under TF-M minimal
pendant.cpu: Arm Cortex-M33 @ 64 MHz, DSP extension present (libopus ARMv5E paths apply)
pendant.ram: 211,608 B application RAM (boards/nrf9160dk_nrf9160_ns.overlay); 32 kB secure, modem shares the first 128 kB
pendant.flash: 1 MB total; application text ~316 kB with libopus at -O3

io.button: ONE user button, devicetree alias sw0. Press starts a conversation; second press ends it. It is also pokable over J-Link for testing.
io.led: ONE LED, alias led0. Currently signals recording, stays solid while agent audio is buffered, and flashes error codes.
io.buses: GPIO, I2C, SPI and I2S all enabled (prj.conf). I2C and SPI are FREE — nothing is attached to them today.
io.caution: There is exactly one I2S peripheral and it runs full duplex (mic in + speaker out) with byte-identical TX/RX config. Any new audio path must share it.

storage.sd: microSD over SPI. CONFIG_DISK_DRIVER_SDMMC, FATFS (ELM) with exFAT enabled. Mount is FS_FATFS.
storage.policy: Owner's standing rule: audio is written to SD ONLY when a chunk upload cannot be uploaded. It is a failure buffer, not a routine store.
storage.note: exFAT means large files and long filenames are available.

audio.mic: I2S microphone, 15,625 Hz capture, Opus-encoded uplink at 16 kHz / 16 kbps, complexity 0
audio.playback: Opus decode on-device at 24 kHz / 60 ms frames, resampled to the 31,250 Hz I2S wire clock, out to the ESP32 bridge
audio.codec: libopus 1.6.1 vendored, fixed-point, built -O3. Decode ~25.4 ms per 60 ms packet; encode ~15.0 ms per call. Roughly 87% of one core when both run.

bridge.board: Adafruit HUZZAH32 (ESP32 classic), 240 MHz dual core, 320 kB DRAM
bridge.role: Receives I2S from the pendant, resamples 31250 -> 44100 with a polyphase FIR, and is an A2DP SOURCE to Bluetooth headphones
bridge.limit: A2DP source is SBC-only and hard-locked to 44.1 kHz stereo in the precompiled bluedroid. RAM is tight: a 44 kB buffer once starved the Bluetooth stack into silence.

network.link: LTE-M (Cat-M1) via the nRF9160 modem. Half duplex in practice.
network.transport: One TLS WebSocket to the Cloudflare Worker carries uplink and downlink audio simultaneously. Modem TLS record limit is about 2 kB.
network.measured: Uplink 16 kbps + downlink 24 kbps saturates the link under contention: a recent call dropped 388 uplink packets (~7.8 s of speech) when the agent was speaking at the same time the owner was.

stack.relay: Cloudflare Worker (Express-style). D1 for jobs/history/memory, R2 for audio. Audio retention 30 days, sweep disabled, ~100 recordings stored.
stack.agent_tools_today: The realtime agent currently has exactly 5 tools: get_mac_status, mac_run_actions, browser_run_actions, web_search, mac_delegate.
stack.mac_harness: A Node "local agent" on the owner's Mac: planner (gpt-5.6-luna), computer-use loop, browser bridge, action risk scoring, atomic JSON store, context graph. It polls /v1/bridge/work for jobs and posts results back.
stack.browser_harness: Driven through the Mac agent's browser bridge today. Cloudflare Browser Run now exists and could give the relay its own server-side browser, removing the Mac from web tasks entirely.
stack.clients: ONE SvelteKit dashboard renders on all three surfaces: web, a Swift menubar app via WKWebView, and iOS via Capacitor pointed at the same Worker URL. A change to the web app ships to all three.
stack.memory: Knowledge-graph style store behind /v1/ops/memory: entities, relations, sessions. Separately, fleetContext.js hand-writes a prompt section per surface, which means adding a surface means editing a prompt.

power.supply: USB or battery. LTE-M transmit bursts draw far more than idle.
power.note: No battery gauge is wired up today, so the agent cannot read charge state.

transcript.text:
Round 6 reconnaissance complete.

### Established
- Mac Local Agent **v0.5.0** is live and reachable on `localhost:8000`; authenticated routes require a Bearer token.
- Cloud relay **v1.1.0** is reachable, paired, and reports the Mac bridge online.
- Browser extension is **offline** with **5 pending commands**.
- Computer-use loop is not ready: Accessibility is untrusted, Screen Recording is missing, and vision upload consent is false.
- Pendant audio remains prototype-grade:
  - Mic: 15,625 Hz capture, Opus uplink at 16 kHz / 16 kbps.
  - Playback: 24 kHz Opus decoded in 60 ms frames, resampled to 31,250 Hz I2S.
  - Encode/decode consume roughly **87% of one Cortex-M33 core together**.
  - LTE-M contention recently dropped **388 uplink packets (~7.8 seconds)**.
- The pendant has exactly one full-duplex I2S peripheral, so any 24 kHz path must share the existing mic/speaker interface.
- ESP32 bridge is SBC-only A2DP at 44.1 kHz and is RAM-constrained.
- SD is intended only as an upload-failure buffer; relay retention is 30 days and sweeping is disabled.
- Owner timezone memory says **America/Chicago**, but live Mac context says **America/New_York**; this needs an explicit precedence rule.

### Still needed to do useful implementation work
1. The previously requested **workspace-edit capability** to modify the firmware/relay audio code.
2. The previously requested **audio-pipeline validation capability** to run end-to-end tests and inspect packet loss, timing, CPU, and playback quality.
3. The previously requested **macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording grants** if GUI/browser validation is required.
4. The pending **24 kHz superwideband acceptance criteria**—especially acceptable latency, packet-loss concealment behavior, CPU ceiling, and audio-quality threshold.

No new side-effecting actions were performed.

result.name: get_mac_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Read live Mac device state: battery, wifi, volume, focused app, or all. Use when the owner asks about battery/charge, wifi/network, volume/mute, or what app is frontmost. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: controlling the Mac (open app, set volume, type, reminders — use mac_run_actions), browser work (browser_run_actions), public web facts (web_search), or multi-step ambiguous tasks (mac_delegate). Never invent readings; always call this tool instead of guessing numbers.

fields.description: Optional status fields to fetch. Omit or use ["all"] for a full snapshot.

spoken_reply.description: Short pendant confirmation (e.g. "Checking battery."). One sentence.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: mac_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE for reversible control. Execute 1–3 concrete Mac actions when the Mac surface is online: open_app, open_url, open_path, create_reminder, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, run_shell (allowlisted system intents), run_applescript, and similar. Prefer high-level types over raw shell when a typed action exists. Use when: owner wants to change or run something on the Mac that is not a pure status read. Do NOT use when: only reading battery/wifi/volume/focused app (get_mac_status), browser page work (browser_run_actions), public facts (web_search), or long multi-step ambiguous workflows (mac_delegate). Confirmation first only for destructive actions. Never claim success without this tool (or get_mac_status) actually queuing work.

actions.description: 1–3 concrete actions for the Mac executor (primary product of this tool).

type.description: Executor action type. Examples: run_shell, run_applescript, create_reminder, open_app, open_url, open_path, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, browser_snapshot, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select.

label.description: Short human-readable label for logs / UI.

params.description: Parameters for the action type. Use only fields that type needs (e.g. command for run_shell, title/due for create_reminder, url for open_url or browser_navigate, selector/text for browser_click/type, appName for open_app matching the Mac software inventory exactly).

spoken_reply.description: Short confirmation for the pendant speaker (preferred user-facing reply).

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure — never block on this; plan from audio via actions.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: get_mac_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Read live Mac device state: battery, wifi, volume, focused app, or all. Use when the owner asks about battery/charge, wifi/network, volume/mute, or what app is frontmost. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: controlling the Mac (open app, set volume, type, reminders — use mac_run_actions), browser work (browser_run_actions), public web facts (web_search), or multi-step ambiguous tasks (mac_delegate). Never invent readings; always call this tool instead of guessing numbers.

fields.description: Optional status fields to fetch. Omit or use ["all"] for a full snapshot.

spoken_reply.description: Short pendant confirmation (e.g. "Checking battery."). One sentence.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: mac_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE for reversible control. Execute 1–3 concrete Mac actions when the Mac surface is online: open_app, open_url, open_path, create_reminder, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, run_shell (allowlisted system intents), run_applescript, and similar. Prefer high-level types over raw shell when a typed action exists. Use when: owner wants to change or run something on the Mac that is not a pure status read. Do NOT use when: only reading battery/wifi/volume/focused app (get_mac_status), browser page work (browser_run_actions), public facts (web_search), or long multi-step ambiguous workflows (mac_delegate). Confirmation first only for destructive actions. Never claim success without this tool (or get_mac_status) actually queuing work.

actions.description: 1–3 concrete actions for the Mac executor (primary product of this tool).

type.description: Executor action type. Examples: run_shell, run_applescript, create_reminder, open_app, open_url, open_path, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, browser_snapshot, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select.

label.description: Short human-readable label for logs / UI.

params.description: Parameters for the action type. Use only fields that type needs (e.g. command for run_shell, title/due for create_reminder, url for open_url or browser_navigate, selector/text for browser_click/type, appName for open_app matching the Mac software inventory exactly).

spoken_reply.description: Short confirmation for the pendant speaker (preferred user-facing reply).

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure — never block on this; plan from audio via actions.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.note: These are the Mac agent routes. Your own backend may differ — probe_http hits whichever backend you run against.

result.name: mac_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE for reversible control. Execute 1–3 concrete Mac actions when the Mac surface is online: open_app, open_url, open_path, create_reminder, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, run_shell (allowlisted system intents), run_applescript, and similar. Prefer high-level types over raw shell when a typed action exists. Use when: owner wants to change or run something on the Mac that is not a pure status read. Do NOT use when: only reading battery/wifi/volume/focused app (get_mac_status), browser page work (browser_run_actions), public facts (web_search), or long multi-step ambiguous workflows (mac_delegate). Confirmation first only for destructive actions. Never claim success without this tool (or get_mac_status) actually queuing work.

actions.description: 1–3 concrete actions for the Mac executor (primary product of this tool).

type.description: Executor action type. Examples: run_shell, run_applescript, create_reminder, open_app, open_url, open_path, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, browser_snapshot, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select.

label.description: Short human-readable label for logs / UI.

params.description: Parameters for the action type. Use only fields that type needs (e.g. command for run_shell, title/due for create_reminder, url for open_url or browser_navigate, selector/text for browser_click/type, appName for open_app matching the Mac software inventory exactly).

spoken_reply.description: Short confirmation for the pendant speaker (preferred user-facing reply).

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure — never block on this; plan from audio via actions.

result.name: get_mac_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Read live Mac device state: battery, wifi, volume, focused app, or all. Use when the owner asks about battery/charge, wifi/network, volume/mute, or what app is frontmost. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: controlling the Mac (open app, set volume, type, reminders — use mac_run_actions), browser work (browser_run_actions), public web facts (web_search), or multi-step ambiguous tasks (mac_delegate). Never invent readings; always call this tool instead of guessing numbers.

fields.description: Optional status fields to fetch. Omit or use ["all"] for a full snapshot.

spoken_reply.description: Short pendant confirmation (e.g. "Checking battery."). One sentence.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.playback: Opus decode on-device at 24 kHz / 60 ms frames, resampled to the 31,250 Hz I2S wire clock, out to the ESP32 bridge
result.codec: libopus 1.6.1 vendored, fixed-point, built -O3. Decode ~25.4 ms per 60 ms packet; encode ~15.0 ms per call. Roughly 87% of one core when both run.

result.board: Adafruit HUZZAH32 (ESP32 classic), 240 MHz dual core, 320 kB DRAM
result.role: Receives I2S from the pendant, resamples 31250 -> 44100 with a polyphase FIR, and is an A2DP SOURCE to Bluetooth headphones
result.limit: A2DP source is SBC-only and hard-locked to 44.1 kHz stereo in the precompiled bluedroid. RAM is tight: a 44 kB buffer once starved the Bluetooth stack into silence.

transcript.text:
Findings this round:

- **Current audio path:** microphone capture is 15,625 Hz PCM, encoded as Opus at 16 kHz/16 kbps; playback decodes Opus at 24 kHz, then resamples to a 31,250 Hz I²S clock before reaching the ESP32 bridge.
- **Bridge limitation:** ESP32 resamples 31,250 → 44,100 Hz and sends SBC-only A2DP at fixed 44.1 kHz stereo. RAM is constrained; a 44 kB buffer previously caused Bluetooth starvation.
- **Live telemetry confirms the target endpoints:** a recent run captured mono 15,625 Hz PCM and rendered mono 24,000 Hz PCM successfully, with zero clipped samples.
- **System status:** relay and Mac bridge are reachable, but Mac readiness is false because Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions remain absent. Browser extension is offline, and the vision loop is disabled.
- **Timezone conflict:** owner memory says `America/Chicago`, while live Mac context says `America/New_York`. I requested clarification and will avoid modifying schedules until resolved.

Still needed to do useful implementation work:

1. The previously requested **workspace-edit capability**, so I can modify firmware/relay sources.
2. The previously requested **audio pipeline validation tool**, to run end-to-end 24 kHz acceptance checks.
3. The previously requested **24 kHz architecture and acceptance criteria** context.
4. Accessibility and Screen Recording grants if GUI inspection or device tooling requires them.

The largest technical unknown is whether “24 kHz superwideband end to end” means only the speech/playback PCM contract, or also requires changing capture, Opus packetization, I²S clocks, and the ESP32/A2DP bridge.

result.name: get_mac_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Read live Mac device state: battery, wifi, volume, focused app, or all. Use when the owner asks about battery/charge, wifi/network, volume/mute, or what app is frontmost. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: controlling the Mac (open app, set volume, type, reminders — use mac_run_actions), browser work (browser_run_actions), public web facts (web_search), or multi-step ambiguous tasks (mac_delegate). Never invent readings; always call this tool instead of guessing numbers.

fields.description: Optional status fields to fetch. Omit or use ["all"] for a full snapshot.

spoken_reply.description: Short pendant confirmation (e.g. "Checking battery."). One sentence.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.name: mac_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE for reversible control. Execute 1–3 concrete Mac actions when the Mac surface is online: open_app, open_url, open_path, create_reminder, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, run_shell (allowlisted system intents), run_applescript, and similar. Prefer high-level types over raw shell when a typed action exists. Use when: owner wants to change or run something on the Mac that is not a pure status read. Do NOT use when: only reading battery/wifi/volume/focused app (get_mac_status), browser page work (browser_run_actions), public facts (web_search), or long multi-step ambiguous workflows (mac_delegate). Confirmation first only for destructive actions. Never claim success without this tool (or get_mac_status) actually queuing work.

actions.description: 1–3 concrete actions for the Mac executor (primary product of this tool).

type.description: Executor action type. Examples: run_shell, run_applescript, create_reminder, open_app, open_url, open_path, type_text, get_volume, set_volume, browser_snapshot, browser_list_tabs, browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select.

label.description: Short human-readable label for logs / UI.

params.description: Parameters for the action type. Use only fields that type needs (e.g. command for run_shell, title/due for create_reminder, url for open_url or browser_navigate, selector/text for browser_click/type, appName for open_app matching the Mac software inventory exactly).

spoken_reply.description: Short confirmation for the pendant speaker (preferred user-facing reply).

transcript.description: Optional short transcript for history/debug only. Omit if unsure — never block on this; plan from audio via actions.

result.name: browser_run_actions
result.description: PROACTIVE when browser work is needed. Execute 1–3 actions through the browser extension when online: browser_list_tabs, browser_snapshot, browser_navigate, browser_click/type by ref, browser_wait_for, browser_read_page, browser_select, scroll. Use when: web/logged-in site work, reading or interacting with a page. Do NOT use when: Mac desktop/system control (mac_run_actions / get_mac_status), public web facts without a page (web_search), or multi-step Mac workflows (mac_delegate). Prefer over Mac desktop control for in-browser tasks.

result.name: relay_job_status
result.description: PROACTIVE. Answer "what happened to the thing I asked you to do on my Mac?" — the status of work ALREADY handed to the Mac, including vague references ("that", "the thing I asked earlier"). Reads the relay job records; needs no Mac round trip, so it answers with the Mac asleep. Call immediately — no confirmation. Do NOT use when: reading live device state such as battery/wifi/volume/frontmost app (get_mac_status), or starting new work (mac_run_actions / mac_delegate). Speak the returned `spoken` sentence essentially verbatim; it already names the task and is sized for the pendant speaker. NEVER upgrade its wording — if it says failed, queued, or unknown, say that; do not report a task as done that this tool did not call done.

reference.description: How the owner referred to the task, in their own words ("that", "the Outlook thing", "what I asked earlier"). Pass it through verbatim; do not invent detail. Omit only if they gave none.

job_id.description: Only when the owner named an exact relay job id. Normally omitted.

transcript.description: Optional history label only. Omit if unsure — never block on this.

result.summary: Enable a bounded audio-retention sweeper and per-job deletion controls: default to short retention for generated briefings, delete expired R2 objects and D1 pointers idempotently, and expose a dashboard ‘delete now’ action. Keep owner-pinned items separate with an explicit expiry.
result.status: proposed
result.note: NOTE RE-DERIVED 2026-08-07. The previous agent's 4,452-char patch plan was DESTROYED when this entry was set to "implementing": scripts/harness-ledger.mjs status --note overwrites the note, it does not append. Every claim below was re-verified against the live files today; the headline claim holds and is worse than it was stated. HEADLINE (TRUE): the sweeper cannot clear a backlog. audioRetention.js:171-175 lists with limit Math.min(Math.max(n,1),100) and passes no cursor; store/jobQuery.js:8 JOB_LIST_MAX_LIMIT = 100 clamps it again, so raising the local constant alone fixes nothing. Ordering is newest-first on both stores (store/d1Store.js:566 ORDER BY created_at DESC; store/memoryStore.js:166). The sweep therefore only ever inspects the 100 NEWEST audio_capture rows — the ones least likely to be expired — and repeated runs never advance the window. A keyset cursor already exists and is plumbed through listJobs({before}) (store/jobQuery.js:19-37, used at server.js:1893); sweepExpiredAudio simply never passes it. OTHER VERIFIED GAPS. (2) AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_MAX_BATCH = 200 at audioRetention.js:32 is unreachable dead config given the 100 cap. (3) No scheduled invocation exists: cloudflare-worker/worker.js exports only fetch, wrangler.jsonc has no crons/triggers, and the sole caller is the manual route at server.js:2151. (4) Inert as shipped: wrangler.jsonc:34 sets AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_ENABLED=false and server.js:2149 forces dryRun, so the deployed sweeper deletes nothing under any input. (5) Bindings are not threaded into either delete path: server.js:2151 and server.js:2834 call without bindings, and cloudflareBindings is only populated inside the Worker fetch handler — under plain Node deleteAudioCaptureObject short-circuits false (audioStorage.js:130-136), so the D1 pointer is cleared at audioRetention.js:141-147 while the R2 object is orphaned permanently, and the response still returns ok:true. (6) Non-atomic ordering: the R2 delete precedes the pointer clear, so an updateJob throw leaves a row addressing a deleted object. (7) In record mode with no store.deleteJob the object is already gone while the row keeps a stale audioRef; that branch has no test. (8) One R2 error aborts the whole sweep: audioRetention.js:195-204 is an unguarded loop with no per-item try/catch and no partial report. (9) NO owner-pin concept exists anywhere in cloud-relay — the entry's "keep owner-pinned items separate with an explicit expiry" is 0% implemented. (10) One global 30-day TTL (config.js:27-31, wrangler.jsonc:33); generated agent audio is an ordinary audio_capture row tagged role:reply (server.js:1075), so "short retention for generated briefings" is not implemented and there is no briefing concept in cloud-relay at all. (11) DELETE /v1/ops/history/:pipelineId/audio (server.js:1979-1995) never follows replyCaptureId, so deleting a run leaves the synthesized reply audio in R2 — and record mode destroys the only reference to it. (12) No dashboard reaches either delete route: src/ops/api.js has no audio DELETE and no retention call at all, so the "dashboard delete now action" does not exist in the frontend. (13) The read-only report at server.js:2115 hardcodes limit 100, so storedRecordings and expiredCount are structurally wrong past 100 captures. (14) The sweep report calls captures.length "scanned" (audioRetention.js:182,209), implying a full-corpus scan that never happened. NO DEFECT FOUND on clock/units: createdAt is ISO-8601 wherever written (jobs.js:20,34-35), parsed with Date.getTime (audioRetention.js:62) and compared against ms Date.now (audioRetention.js:78,86); maxAgeMs is milliseconds in config.js:27, in wrangler.jsonc:33 (2592000000 = 30d) and in the comparison alike. TEST GAPS: audioRetention.test.js never exercises a backlog >100 through a real store (the batch-cap test calls selectExpiredAudioCaptures on a plain array, bypassing listJobs, so gap 1 is invisible to the suite and gap 2 is asserted as correct), never makes an R2 delete throw, and always passes bindings explicitly — which is precisely what production does not do. cloud-relay/ was NOT edited. Left proposed.

result.summary: Add a durable browser job runner with two backends: the authenticated Safari bridge for owner-private pages and Cloudflare Browser Run for public pages. Represent each step as navigate/read/extract/click/type, persist evidence (URL, title, timestamp, selected text), retry transient failures, and expose a job result stream to the planner.
result.status: proposed
result.note: KEPT OPEN: the backend ROUTER now exists, the durable job runner still does not. Backend A ships: local-agent/browserSessions.js (chg-bc35ae04 / chg-2fffc681 / chg-086a6904). Backend B ships: cloud-relay/serverBrowser.js (chg-81e5c92d, implemented). ROUTER DONE 2026-08-07 — local-agent/originFanOut.js chooseBackend() is the selector this entry named: owner-private -> Safari (only it holds the sessions); public -> Browser Run (only it is awake when the Mac sleeps); LAN / private IP / localhost -> Safari only, decided by serverBrowser.normalizePublicUrl rather than a second copy of that logic; relay budget spent -> Safari; explicit backend:"safari"|"relay" always honoured. An owner-private page is deliberately NOT failed over to the relay when Safari is down: the relay cannot hold the session, so the trip buys a login wall at the price of one of ten daily browser-minutes, and reserving that budget is what keeps the public leg answerable. Free-tier limits are enforced rather than documented: relay lane is serial, paced to 1 action per 10s, and a UTC-day browser-ms tally persists in .pendant-relay-browser-budget.json (GET /origins/budget). MISSING STILL: no durable job runner — no jobId, no persistence across a restart, no retry of transient failures — and no job result stream to the planner. serverBrowser is still unreachable from the voice path (chg-f527c3bc, unapplied wiring diff).
